item.title: Autism shapes social integration and reciprocity in elementary classrooms
item.description: Research question How does neurodevelopmental diversity — specifically autism — shape the structure of social networks and reciprocal peer relationships in elementary classrooms? Main contribution This paper introduces a novel ecological approach using experimental game theory to quantify social integration and reciprocity among autistic children in real classroom settings. Social networks were constructed from children’s peer selections in a distributive game played on networked tablets, capturing revealed social preferences rather than self-reports.

item.title: School schedules and mothers' employment
item.description: Research question What happens to mothers’ labor outcomes when schools move from half-day to full-day schedules? Main contribution Using panel data and quasi-experimental variation from an education reform in Chile, we find positive effects on labor force participation, employment, hours worked, and months worked. Published in Review of Economics of the Household, 2023. Abstract Women’s employment plays an important role in household well-being, and among mothers, lack of child care is one of the main reasons for not working and not seeking employment.

item.title: Reciprocity heightens academic performance in elementary school students
item.description: Research question How are students’ social reciprocity patterns related to academic achievement? Main contribution Using data from 855 students across 14 public schools in Chile, we show that reciprocity in peer relationships is associated with better grades, including in a difference-in-differences design across semesters. Published in Heliyon (Cell Press), 2022. Abstract Social relationships are pivotal for human beings. Yet, we still lack a complete understanding of the types and conditions of social relationships that facilitate learning among children.
